This event is generated when a logon session is created. It is generated on the computer that was accessed.

rule.description: Powershell script querying system environment variables

system.message:
"Creating Scriptblock text (1 of 1):
#requires -RunAsAdministrator
# ==================================================================
# SOC Triage - FINAL Windows Collection Run (WIN-CL1)
# Known + novel techniques, matched to the Linux run for cross-platform.
# Loops for volume; anchors on the pwsh session ProcessGuid; UTC markers.
#
# RUN AS (elevated pwsh):
#   .\collect_win.ps1 *>&1 | Tee-Object -FilePath C:\atomic\collect_markers_win.txt
#
# PREREQ: Sysmon running (Get-Service Sysmon* -> Running).
# ==================================================================

$Rounds   = 6
$Gap      = 8      # seconds between attacks
$Dwell    = 18     # seconds to leave artifacts for detection
$Baseline = 90     # quiet baseline between rounds
$Target   = "127.0.0.1"

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path C:\atomic | Out-Null

function Mark($status, $detail) {
    $ts = (Get-Date).ToUniversalTime().ToString("yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ssZ")
    Write-Output ">>> $ts $status | $detail"

	Source Port:		63533

	Authentication Package:	NTLM
	Transited Services:	-
	Package Name (NTLM only):	-
	Key Length:		0

This event is generated when a logon request fails. It is generated on the computer where access was attempted.

	- Transited services indicate which intermediate services have participated in this logon request.
	- Package name indicates which sub-protocol was used among the NTLM protocols.
	- Key length indicates the length of the generated session key. This will be 0 if no session key was requested."
